summary.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast to divest JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms plus Daund rail for INR1,154 crore, with INR500 crore due around January 2027.
summary.overview: Management, on an investor call held October 7, 2026, outlined the sale of the LST (liquid storage tank) businesses at JNPA, Goa and Cochin, together with the JNPA-linked Daund rail business, for INR1,154 crore plus an exit-linked consideration. Payment is staged: about INR500 crore by January 2027, about INR300 crore by March 2027, and the balance INR354 crore over 12 to 18 months tied to port approvals and tank commissioning. Of the first INR500 crore, about INR190-200 crore goes to tax and bank-limit closure and about INR200 crore to a buyback and special dividend, with INR100 crore for chemical expansion and EPC book growth. Management guided chemical PAT to about INR18 crore in FY26 rising to INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years, and EPC PAT to about INR150 crore by around FY30. Much of the Q&A probed the rationale for exiting the higher-margin LST business and the lack of quarter-wise numbers.

segments.name: LST (liquid tank farm) – divested
segments.commentary: JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms and JNPA-linked Daund rail are being sold for INR1,154 crore. JNPA expected in books until about Dec 2026/Jan 2027, with Cochin and Goa removed gradually over the next calendar year. Company retains a small stake in a Kandla terminal, described as insignificant; a non-compete applies.

segments.name: Chemical (benzoic acid, sodium benzoate)
segments.commentary: Two plants, each about 1,000 tons/month; utilisation about 70-80%. One plant is being doubled, with completion expected July 2027. REACH certification obtained for UK and EU; orders over 600 tons received, expected to reach about 2,000 tons/year. Management targets chemical PAT of INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years.

segments.name: EPC (tankage, pipeline, petroleum)
segments.commentary: Order book expected to be about INR500-600 crore next year, with EPC revenue of about INR250 crore per annum from FY28 onward per management. Targeted 5% share of a INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum-related EPC opportunity implies about INR150 crore PAT. EBITDA margin assumption 7-8% on a conservative basis, PAT margin basis not clearly specified.

guidance_outlook: Chemical PAT expected to be INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years (from INR18 crore in FY26); management says chemical profitability to rise 3-4x in 4-5 years.
EPC PAT of about INR150 crore targeted by around 2030, assuming 5% share of INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum EPC pipeline.
Total PAT target of about INR210 crore in 3-5 years versus about INR70 crore currently; FY28 PAT growth target of 15-20% YoY.
Chemical revenue to rise about 20-25% in the year after capacity commissioning and about 70-80% in the following year, per management.
Debt expected to stay at minimum; company does not expect to need significant bank debt, although bank limits are needed for guarantees.
Further tranche proceeds to be used for expansion or shareholder returns, decided by the board based on capex visibility.
capex_capacity: Chemical capacity doubling at one plant (of two, about 1,000 tons/month each), targeted completion July 2027.
Stage 1 capex across chemical and EPC of not more than about INR150 crore.
New agro and specialty derivative plants planned with technology and licence partners; to be funded later, with back-to-back buyback arrangements with customers under discussion.
Management says no balance capex remains on the JNPA port asset, and that about 43 tanks are under construction at JNPA (per management answer on LST growth capex).
Capex to continue over the next 1-2 years; first stage expected to be complete by FY28.
demand_pricing: REACH certification enabled UK and EU exports; over 600 tons of orders received.
Management says the chemical business profit grew from INR5 crore (FY24) to INR15-16 crore (FY25), INR18 crore (FY26) with turnover broadly flat.
Crude-linked raw material costs: management says it passes through fluctuations to customers but cannot rule out margin impact at high crude prices.
Chemical EBITDA margin cited by analyst at 11-12%; management expects to sustain or improve it without a firm number.
EPC contract wins include KKR (about INR300 crore), GACL/NALCO JV pipeline, ANA Oleo, Allana, Adani MPL and Jindal projects.
